![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14004888/assets/09482b1e9903bff25b16b2239975831e6d54440a8f8ea78f5739b0eafee3d9e8.png)

Find the area between the curve $y=-2{x}^{2}-x+3$, the $x$-axis and the $y$-axis, shown above.
questions.worked_solution:
To find the area, we just need to compute the corresponding definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(-2{x}^{2}-x+3)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x-1{\int }_{0}^{1}x\,\text{d}x+3{\int }_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2\cdot {\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}|}_{0}^{1}-1\cdot {\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}|}_{0}^{1}+3x{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =-2(\frac{1}{3}-0)-1(\frac{1}{2}-0)+3(1-0) \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}-\frac{1}{2}+3 \\  & =\frac{11}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

A region is bounded by the curve $y={e}^{x}$ and the $x$-axis between $x=-\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)$ and $x=\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)$, as shown above. Find the area $A$ of the region. Do not round the answer.

$A=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
To find the area, we just need to compute the corresponding definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}{e}^{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={e}^{x}{|}_{-\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)} \\  & ={e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}-{e}^{-\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)} \\  & =2-\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

A region is bounded by the curve $y=-2{x}^{2}+3$ and the $x$-axis between $x=0$ and $x=1$, as shown above. Find the area $A$ of the region. Do not round the answer.

$A=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
To find the area, we just need to compute the corresponding definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(-2{x}^{2}+3)\,\text{d}x \\  & =(-2\cdot \frac{{x}^{3}}{3}+3x){|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(-\frac{2}{3}+3)-0 \\  & =\frac{7}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

The area of the shaded region between the curve $y={x}^{3}+8$ and the $x$-axis is given by the integral expression below. What is the value of $a?$

$$
A={\int }_{a}^{2}({x}^{3}+8)\,\text{d}x.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
To get $a$, we need to find the $x$-intercepts of the curve $y={x}^{3}+8.$ 

We solve the equation for $y=0$: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{3}+8 & =y \\ {x}^{3}+8 & =0 \\ {x}^{3} & =-8 \\ x & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $a=-2.$

A region in the $x$-$y$ plane is bounded by the curve $y={sec}^{2}⁡x+\frac{1}{x}$, and the $x$-axis between $x=\frac{\pi }{6}$ and $x=\frac{\pi }{3}$, as shown above. 
Find the area $A$ of the region. Do not round the answer.

$A=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
To find the area, we just need to compute the corresponding definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3}({sec}^{2}⁡(x)+\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3}{sec}^{2}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x\,+\,{\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3}\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(\operatorname{tan}⁡(x)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)){|}_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3} \\  & =(\operatorname{tan}⁡\frac{\pi }{3}+\operatorname{ln}⁡\frac{\pi }{3})-(\operatorname{tan}⁡\frac{\pi }{6}+\operatorname{ln}⁡\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =\sqrt{3}+\operatorname{ln}⁡\frac{\pi }{3}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}-\operatorname{ln}⁡\frac{\pi }{6} \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}+\operatorname{ln}⁡\frac{\pi /3}{\pi /6} \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}+\operatorname{ln}⁡(2).\end{aligned}
$$

A region is bounded by the curve $y=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}$, the $x$-axis, and the lines $x=-0.5$ and $x=0.5$, as shown above. What is the area of the region?
questions.worked_solution:
To find the area, we just need to compute the corresponding definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-0.5}^{0.5}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{\int }_{-0.5}^{0.5}\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x{|}_{-0.5}^{0.5} \\  & =-(\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(0.5)-\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(-0.5)) \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{6}+(-\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we obtained a negative number. So the area that we want is $\frac{\pi }{3}.$

A region is bounded by the curve $y=\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and the $x$-axis between $x=-\pi $ and $x=0$, as shown above. What is the area of the region?
questions.worked_solution:
To find the area, we just need to compute the corresponding definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\pi }^{0}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡x{|}_{-\pi }^{0} \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)-(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\pi )) \\  & =-1-(1) \\  & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we obtained a negative number. So the area that we want is $2.$

A region is bounded by the curve $y=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}}$, the $x$-axis, and the lines $x=-1$ and $x=1$, as shown above. Find the area $A$ of the region. Do not round the answer.

$A=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
To find the area, we just need to compute the corresponding definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{\int }_{-1}^{1}\frac{1}{\sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-arcsin\,(\frac{x}{2}){|}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =-(arcsin\,(\frac{1}{2})-arcsin\,(-\frac{1}{2})) \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{6}+(-\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we obtained a negative number. So the area that we want is 

$$
A=-{\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x=\frac{\pi }{3}.
$$

Find the area between the curve $y=-{x}^{2}-1$, the $x$-axis, and the line $x=-1$ and $x=1$ (shown above). Do not round the answer.

$A=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
To find the area, we just need to compute the corresponding definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}(-{x}^{2}-1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{\int }_{-1}^{1}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x-{\int }_{-1}^{1}\text{d}x \\  & =-{\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}|}_{-1}^{1}-x{|}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =-(\frac{1}{3}-\frac{(-1)^{3}}{3})-(1-(-1)) \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}-2 \\  & =-\frac{8}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we obtained a negative number. So the area that we want is 

$$
A=-{\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x=\frac{8}{3}.
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Find the area between the curve $y=x^2-2x+2,$ the $x$-axis, and the lines $x=0$ and $x=2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14004888/assets/6b85f10cde49017eac1c56ad1b8abbcdf3033a367d5e1eb162dd89fbb6141461.png)
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To find the area, we just need to compute the corresponding definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}({x}^{2}-2x+2)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x-2{\int }_{0}^{2}x\,\text{d}x+2{\int }_{0}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}|}_{0}^{2}-2\cdot {\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}|}_{0}^{2}+2x{|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =(\frac{8}{3}-0)-2(2-0)+2(2-0) \\  & =\frac{8}{3}-4+4 \\  & =\frac{8}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Find the area of the closed region between the curve $y=x^2-1$ and the $x$-axis.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we find the intersections of the curve with the $x$-axis:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-1 & =0 \\ {x}^{2} & =1 \\ x & =\pm 1.\end{aligned}
$$

We draw a sketch of the region, as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14004888/assets/9b78aad41f84f6a6997914bd8d4243f30cb0ebea4edb5305962dc11c7a46a807.png)

We want the area between the curve $y=x^2-1$ and the $x$-axis, from $x=-1$ to $x=1.$ To find the area, we just need to compute the corresponding definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}({x}^{2}-1)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x-{\int }_{-1}^{1}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}|}_{-1}^{1}-x{|}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{1}{3}-(-\frac{1}{3}))-(1-(-1)) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}-2 \\  & =-\frac{4}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we obtained a negative number. So the area that we want is $\dfrac{4}{3}.$
